prompt:
Use the attached clay render as the exact blueprint. Keep every wall, opening, window, cornice, skirting, floor and ceiling line, the camera height, lens and angle, and the position, size and angle of every furniture piece and built-in exactly as in the clay. Move, resize, add or remove nothing. Each placeholder shape in the clay marks one product listed below; render it there at the stated size. Only turn the clay into real materials and light. The other attached images are close-ups of the exact products: match their form, colour and texture. Positions are fractions of frame width (x) and height (y) from the top-left.

1. PHOTO. Editorial interior for a top design magazine: a Nordic kitchen-dining room, 3 pm mid-winter, 24 mm shift lens at 1.1 m, level, straight verticals, all sharp. Hero: the oak table under the big lantern on the left third, the calm kitchen behind.

2. LIGHT. Only key: diffuse daylight from the east window at the left edge, no direct sun. Exposed for the walls: the wall beside the window reads clean warm white, just under the glowing reveals; the glass one step brighter and still detailed, a pale winter garden. Light falls off toward the far corner. Each piece has a lit left face and a right side about one stop darker; the furniture throws long feathered shadows to the right and toward the camera, short dense contact shadows. The ceiling a touch darker than the walls. White balance 4600 K: warm white, never pink, yellow or grey; real contrast, never milky. Practicals 2700 K, low, no shadows: the lantern glows from within and lays a soft warm pool on the table, about as wide as the table is deep; hidden LED strips under both shelves wash the upstand softly.

3. MATERIALS. Walls matte mineral paint #F4F1EC. Floor wide oiled white-oak planks, pale honey #D6BF9E. Table (rounded top, tapered legs), chairs, bench, shelves: oiled oak #C8A27A with a soft satin sheen, one long soft window highlight along the table top and down the planks, no mirror reflection. Kitchen: flat handleless warm-white matte fronts, honed light limestone counter and upstand, warm-white lime-plaster hood, matte black tap.

4. PRODUCTS, exactly these:
a. LANTERN x 0.26-0.39, y 0.13-0.25: flat round cloth lantern 50 wide, 36 high, taut warm off-white cloth between thin matte black ribs and rings, under a third of the table's length, bottom 75 cm above the table.
b. RUNNER: stone-washed oat linen 40 x 140, soft crumple, plain hem, no fringe, along the table axis.
c. VASE on the runner under the lantern: 26 cm warm-white matte stoneware, fine stone texture, half the lantern's width; 3-5 olive sprigs.
d. CANDLES left of the vase: two flat matte black iron plates, palm-sized, unlit warm-white pillar candles 15 and 10 cm, the taller under two thirds of the vase.
e. CURTAIN x 0.16-0.20: one sheer natural linen-blend panel #EDE7DB, narrow S-fold stack, slim black rod, hem on the floor, backlit.
f. BENCH PAD: off-white linen-look cushion, 3 cm thin, the full bench length.
g. RUG under table and chairs, cut by the bottom edge: flat hand-woven off-white wool, visible loom slub.
h. LEFT SHELF: a 30 x 40 portrait print leaning on the wall, taupe block and black line on white, thin black frame, a third of the hood's width; nothing else on that shelf.
i. COUNTER right of the hob: two light-oak pepper mills, shorter than the tap; a 21 cm warm-white matte bowl, low, three russet pears.
j. RIGHT SHELF: a stack of four matte grey-sand plates, no taller than a mug; three sandy stoneware mugs, cream rims, half the mills' height.
k. FLOOR before the counter: a 60 x 280 ivory wool runner, low pile, thin line border.

5. NOT IN FRAME: floor vase, kitchen wall lamp, sink set, utensil jar, cutting boards, plants, other food, appliances, books, glass, text, people. No sun patches, beams, bloom, haze, glow halos, HDR look, grain or vignette.
